title: Implementation of QR factorization of tall and very skinny matrices on current GPUs
summary: We consider the problem of computing a QR (or QZ) decomposition of a real, dense, tall and very skinny matrix. That is, the number of columns is tiny compared to the number of rows, rendering most computations completely or partially memory-bandwidth limited. The paper focuses on recent NVIDIA GPGPUs still supporting 64-bit floating-point arithmetic, but the findings carry over to AMD GPUs as well. We discuss two basic algorithms: Methods based on the normal equations (Gram matrix), in particular Cholesky-QR2 and SVQB, and the "tall-skinny QR" (TSQR), based on Householder transformations in…
